title: 2月第三套 · Verbal 2（15 题）
objectives: 按真实考试节奏做完 15 题（建议 23 分钟），**全部做完再点提交**（提交前不显示对错）
提交后逐题看对错和正确答案；错题先回原文找依据，再决定是词汇问题还是逻辑问题

pass: The post-1850 economic boom in the United States had its greatest impact on eastern mill towns, such as Lowell. Massachusetts. Formerly peaceful villages became bustling towns whose factories rose to dominate their skylines. Their populations sometimes tripled in a decade, forcing property less workers into overcrowded, dilapidated housing. Their economies came under the domination of industrialists who competed unfairly with one another and were contemptuous of the old ways. These industrialists had economic power and the social and political power that accompanied it; town politicians catered to their interests. Other property owners, especially small-business entrepreneurs and professionals, identified with them and applauded their successes. The factory workers inevitably found themselves alienated from property owners and helpless before their employers. Thus, economic class, social status, and power were inextricably intertwined; control over property and machinery was readily

possess political and social power
increase significantly the prosperity of eastern mill town residents
find their power resisted by property less workers
compete with the interests of the propertied business and professional classes

pass: Scientists have long debated the exact timing of the lunar cataclysm, a period approximately 4 billion years ago when Earth and the Moon were pummeled with asteroids. A clue to this puzzle may come from spherules, millimeter-sized droplets of molten rock formed after an asteroid collides explosively with a planet. Upon impact, the asteroid vaporizes both itself and the target rock, producing a vapor plume that condenses into spherules. These form a layer preserved in rock, whose age can be estimated using radiometric dating. Scientists know of fourteen of these spherule layers scattered across Earth, but none dates to the theorized lunar cataclysm time period.
